title: The silent-undo check judges a lane from its merge base, so a branch that predates a main move does not read as undoing it
why: Coordinator 14:56 CST Nov 8: after batch 65 moved main to 2ac382cc6, lane lint's silent-undo check fails PRs that merely predate the move. #1471 at fae2e9d0b reads "docs/debts/notes.md: hunk reversed, undoing 2ac382cc6"; #2024, #2034, #2253 and #1860 will hit it too. Suspected cause: the check compares the lane head with main's tip, not with its merge base. Reproduce first. If so, it is a false-alarm fix: judge the lane's own changes from the merge base, and keep refusing a real undo (a lane that merged main and reverted a hunk). Related: step silent-undo-merged-main.
note: Coordinator 14:58 CST Nov 8: the premise is wrong for #1471. A real merge re-adds notes rows that batch 65 retired, so the check is right there (decision silent-undo-check-design). The lane measures #2024, #2034, #2253 and #1860, and closes this step if none is a false alarm.
